title: Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) on Broadway #twostranger...
transcript: Two Strangers is easily the early frontrunner for next year's Best Musical. It's a real charmer that has all the makings of a hit — good music, lovely performances, emotional substance, and maybe most charming of all, it's unexpected. It's a two-person musical with an unconventional plot. Dougal from London visits New York for his father's wedding, spending the weekend helping the bride's sister Robin with some last minute errands. As a jaded Brooklynite, she initially finds his starry-eyed, golden retriever energy grating, but gradually loosens up to his vibe. You can immediately root for both of these characters — in fact, it's actually hard not to when they're portrayed with the level of charisma and humanity that Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts bring to the table. There's a fantastic synergy going on between the performances, the material, and the direction that makes the show really funny and entertaining, but also deeply attuned to the various tone shifts throughout. In addition to the story, the production is very well done. The scenic design inventively repurposes two stacks of luggage for pretty much everything under the sun, and I love how everything is practical. Instead of going for a series of cheap projections to create a literal sense of time and place, they opted for a significantly more inspired and gestural design. Not only does this give the actors more of a playground, but it indicates a level of trust in the material and the performances — that there's no need to swallow them up with visual grandeur to keep the audience's attention. They had us in their hands from start to finish, and it was like a breath of fresh air. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
